1	\begin{abstract}
2	Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models encode observations as hundreds of vision tokens, creating a computational bottleneck for real-time robotic control. Token pruning offers a training-free remedy, yet its effect varies dramatically across architectures: at retention ratio $k{=}0.95$, $\pi_{0.5}$ preserves 98\% task success while SmolVLA collapses to 0\%---why?
3	
4	We identify the vision-language connector as the primary architectural factor governing pruning tolerance. The coefficient of variation (CV) of post-connector token norms, computable in a single forward pass, predicts compressibility across the full architecture spectrum: from CV$\,{=}\,$0.038 (near-immune linear projection) to CV$\,{=}\,$0.314 (catastrophic pixel-shuffle collapse). Across five VLA architectures (450\,M--7\,B parameters) and four LIBERO manipulation suites, token-independent connectors degrade gracefully, while token-entangling connectors exhibit abrupt cliffs: SmolVLA collapses when just 6 of 128 tokens are removed.
5	
6	Importance-based selection is not universally beneficial---it can be actively harmful. L2 norm selection preserves 98\% success on $\pi_{0.5}$ where random yields 5\% (93\,pp gap); at aggressive ratios, random outperforms L2 by up to 36\,pp. No scoring method is universally safe: task complexity amplifies connector-dependent patterns ($20{\times}$ from Object to Goal). A zero-mask ablation isolates the mechanism: zeroing 10\% of tokens preserves 98.0\% SR while physical removal collapses to 9.0\%---the 89\,pp gap is entirely attributable to position disruption, not information loss. For architectures where all deletion fails, a lightweight re-encoding module (${\sim}$5\% extra parameters) recovers $>$60\% success at 75\% compression.
7	\end{abstract}

lines: CV predicts connector-level compressibility, but task complexity determines \emph{which} scoring method succeeds within a given connector---L2 leads on $\pi_{0.5}$ Object but inverts on Long; on X-VLA, attention recovers near-baseline while L2 is anti-informative (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}). The V-shaped random recovery on $\pi_{0.5}$ Long reflects position encoding sensitivity: scattered gaps maximally disrupt RoPE at $k{\approx}0.9$, recovering as surviving positions become approximately uniform.

-Connector architecture is the primary factor governing VLA token compressibility. Token-independent connectors degrade gracefully; entangling connectors exhibit catastrophic cliffs amplified by task complexity ($20{\times}$ from Object to Goal). CV partitions models in a single forward pass. Under sufficient compression, scoring effectiveness becomes connector- and $k$-dependent. Where all deletion fails, VTR recovers over 60\% SR at 75\% compression. Real-robot validation and adaptive per-task pruning schedules remain open.

input.old_string: All evaluations use LIBERO simulation; no sim-to-real evidence is provided. The six architectures differ in backbone, encoder, and scale beyond the connector, preventing full causal isolation of the connector effect. The CV--SR correlation relies on four closed-loop models, too few for a general law. VTR is validated on SmolVLA only. Most conditions use a single seed; $\pi_{0.5}$ Long uses five-seed means ($n{=}5$, s.d.\ ${\leq}$2.7\,pp). \textbf{AI disclosure:} This work used AI tools (Claude) for code development and manuscript drafting; all scientific claims are the authors' own.
input.new_string: All evaluations use LIBERO simulation; no sim-to-real evidence is provided; real-robot evaluation with domain shift would strengthen practical applicability. The six architectures differ in backbone, encoder, and scale beyond the connector, preventing full causal isolation of the connector effect; controlled studies varying only the connector within a fixed backbone would sharpen causal claims. The CV--SR correlation relies on four closed-loop models, too few for a general law; expanding the model pool as new VLA architectures emerge will test whether CV generalizes as a universal diagnostic. VTR is validated on SmolVLA only; extending to other entangling connectors (e.g., cross-attention encoders) would test generality of the re-encoding approach. Only L2-norm and random scoring are systematically compared; gradient-based importance scoring or learned pruning masks could yield better token selection. Most conditions use a single seed; $\pi_{0.5}$ Long uses five-seed means ($n{=}5$, s.d.\ ${\leq}$2.7\,pp); future work should adopt multi-seed evaluation across all conditions to quantify variance. \textbf{AI disclosure:} This work used AI tools (Claude) for code development and manuscript drafting; all scientific claims are the authors' own.
